summary: Anthropic reports that the US government's export controls on Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 (imposed June 12 after a reported safeguard bypass) have been lifted as of June 30, restoring global access to Fable 5 and partial access to Mythos 5, and details new safeguards, a proposed industry jailbreak-severity framework, and deeper government collaboration commitments.

mechanisms.reason: The document describes the US government both imposing and then lifting export controls that forced Anthropic to suspend and later restore global access to two frontier models.
mechanisms.quote: On Friday, June 12, the US government applied export controls to our newest models, Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5. This required us to restrict access to foreign nationals, whether inside or outside the United States.

mechanisms.reason: Access to both models, previously suspended for all users worldwide, is being restored, reversing an inference-volume-suppressing suspension.
mechanisms.quote: Access to Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 is now restored ... Fable 5 will be available starting tomorrow, Wednesday, July 1, to users globally on the Claude Platform, Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork.

practices.reason: Teams building on Fable 5 need to plan for usage-limit changes, blocked-request rerouting to Opus 4.8, and a phased credit-based access schedule with a hard July 7 date.
practices.quote: For Pro, Max, Team, and select Enterprise plans, 1 Fable 5 will be included for up to 50% of weekly usage limits through July 7, after which it will be available via usage credits .

notable_reason: A frontier lab's flagship models were suspended globally under a US government export control order and then restored, alongside a new cross-industry jailbreak severity framework and deepened government pre-release testing commitments -- a first-of-its-kind regulatory episode for the sector.
